content: 1. Piretanone reduces the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of lamotrigine by enhancing hepatic clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Combination oral contraceptives significantly lower lamotrigine plasma levels, likely due to the induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Monitor patients for reduced lamotrigine efficacy. 3. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while levalbuterol decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 4. Drospirenone reduces the effects of liraglutide by altering passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Exercise caution and monitor therapy. 5. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 6. The combination of lisinopril and drospirenone poses a risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor potassium levels. 7. Drospirenone decreases the efficacy of lonapegsomatropin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may also reduce the serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, potentially necessitating higher growth hormone doses. Monitor therapy closely. 8. Drospirenone and lornoxicam both increase serum potassium levels. Adjust therapy and monitor potassium levels closely. 9. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Monitor therapy closely. 10. Drospirenone and various NSAIDs (e.g., meloxicam, naproxen, piroxicam) increase serum potassium levels. Adjust therapy and monitor potassium levels closely. 11. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while beta-agonists like metaproterenol and terbutaline decrease it. The clinical significance of these interactions is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 12. Drospirenone reduces the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exercise caution and monitor therapy. 13. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while diuretics like methyclothiazide and metolazone decrease it. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 14. Drospirenone and beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol, nadolol, propranolol) increase serum potassium levels. Adjust therapy and monitor potassium levels closely. 15. Drospirenone's efficacy is reduced by mifepristone due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution, and consider a backup contraceptive method. 16. Drospirenone and ACE inhibitors (e.g., moexipril, perindopril, ramipril) increase the risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor potassium levels. 17. Drospirenone increases serum potassium when combined with ARBs (e.g., losartan, valsartan, telmisartan). Adjust therapy and monitor potassium levels closely. 18. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of CYP3A4 substrates (e.g., abemaciclib, alprazolam, atorvastatin) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 19. Drospirenone decreases the level or effect of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 20. Aspirin reduces the level or effect of drospirenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 21. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of growth hormone analogs (e.g., somatropin, somatrogon) by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce IGF-1 response, necessitating higher growth hormone doses. Monitor therapy closely. 22. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of various drugs (e.g., apixaban, amiodarone, bosutinib) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 23. Drospirenone increases serum potassium when combined with potassium-sparing agents (e.g., potassium citrate, potassium iodide). Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 25. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of hydrocodone (via benzhydrocodone) when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of various anticancer agents (e.g., bortezomib, brentuximab vedotin) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 27. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 28. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 29. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 30. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 31. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of benzphetamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 32. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 33. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 34. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy. 35. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown; monitor therapy.
